content: GPR112, also known as G protein-coupled receptor 112, is a protein encoded by the ADGRG4 gene. This receptor belongs to the adhesion G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) family. Adhesion GPCRs are distinguished by their extended extracellular regions, which frequently contain N-terminal protein modules. These modules are connected to a seven-transmembrane (TM7) region through a specialized domain called the GPCR-Autoproteolysis INducing (GAIN) domain. GPR112 is expressed in human enterochromaffin cells and is also found in the mouse intestine. The N-terminal fragment (NTF) of GPR112 includes pentraxin (PTX)-like modules. Additionally, the expression of the GPR112 gene has been identified as a marker for neuroendocrine carcinoma cells.
